policy_name: Inflation Reduction Act Section 11406: $35 Monthly Cap on Medicare Part D Insulin Cost Sharing

fields.name: monthly_cost_sharing_cap
fields.description: Maximum enrollee cost sharing for a one-month supply of a covered insulin product, effective January 1, 2023.
fields.scope: All Medicare Part D enrollees using covered insulin products
fields.causal_relevance: Sets the primary cost-sharing limit that sponsors must implement at the point of sale, directly determining enrollee out-of-pocket costs and the basis for the retrospective subsidy.

evidence.evidence_quote: cost sharing for a one-month supply of each covered insulin product must not exceed $35 for all enrollees in all coverage phases.

fields.name: reimbursement_deadline_days
fields.description: Number of calendar days within which Part D sponsors must reimburse enrollees for any cost-sharing amount charged above $35 during the transition period.
fields.scope: Part D sponsors charging higher cost sharing during the transition period
fields.causal_relevance: Establishes the compliance burden for sponsors during the transition period, affecting their administrative processes and potential penalties for non-compliance.

evidence.evidence_quote: the plan must reimburse enrollees within 30 calendar days any cost-sharing amount charged to the enrollee that exceeds $35 for a one-month supply of a covered insulin product.

policy_parameters.name: effective_date
policy_parameters.description: Date when the cost-sharing limits become effective for all Part D plans.

evidence.evidence_quote: These changes become effective January 1, 2023 and apply to all Part D plans, including Employer Group Waiver plans.

policy_parameters.name: transition_period_end
policy_parameters.description: End of the transition period during which sponsors may charge higher cost sharing if they reimburse enrollees.

evidence.evidence_quote: if a Part D sponsor is unable to do so and charges higher cost sharing between January 1, 2023 through March 31, 2023 based on its previously approved CY 2023 PBP, the plan must reimburse enrollees within 30 calendar days any cost-sharing amount charged to the enrollee that exceeds $35 for a one-month supply of a covered insulin product.

policy_parameters.name: deductible_not_applicable
policy_parameters.description: The deductible shall not apply to covered insulin products.

evidence.evidence_quote: the deductible shall not apply to covered insulin products, and cost sharing for a one-month supply of each covered insulin product must not exceed $35 for all enrollees in all coverage phases.

policy_parameters.name: out_of_network_differential_cap
policy_parameters.description: Total cost sharing for a one-month supply of a covered insulin product, inclusive of any out-of-network differential, must not exceed $35.

evidence.evidence_quote: in no event may a plan require an enrollee to pay more than $35 in total cost sharing for a one-month supply of a covered insulin product, inclusive of any OON differential charged to the enrollee.

policy_parameters.name: lis_category_4_threshold
policy_parameters.description: LIS cost sharing that exceeds $35 (e.g., LIS Category 4) is eligible for the temporary retrospective subsidy.

evidence.evidence_quote: the temporary retrospective subsidy is available for any applicable LIS cost sharing that exceeds $0 for ACIPrecommended vaccines and any applicable LIS cost sharing that exceeds $35 (e.g., LIS Category 4) but is less than the plan’s cost sharing, as reflected in the CY 2023 PBP, for covered insulin products.

summary: Document-grounded initial state. Inputs: monthly_cost_sharing_cap=35 USD; reimbursement_deadline_days=30 days. Fixed policy parameters: effective_date=2023-01-01 date; transition_period_end=2023-03-31 date; deductible_not_applicable=True boolean; out_of_network_differential_cap=35 USD; lis_category_4_threshold=35 USD.
